title: waktu — when
pattern: Waktu A, B · B waktu A · waktu kecil
explanation: waktu (literally time) introduces a particular time, usually in the past: Waktu saya di Bali, cuacanya panas sekali. — When I was in Bali, the weather was really hot. It can come first, with a comma, or after the main part: Saya kenal suami saya waktu kuliah. waktu kecil means as a child: Waktu kecil, saya tinggal dekat pantai. ketika means the same and is more common in writing and storytelling; in casual speech you'll hear pas (Pas aku sampai, …).
natural: Talking about your past: where you lived, how you met someone, what happened on a trip. Fine in any conversation.
stiff: For the future, or for whenever, kalau is the natural choice: Kalau sudah sampai, kabari saya. With waktu that sounds as if it has already happened. And on its own waktu is also the noun time: Saya tidak ada waktu.

examples.indonesian: Waktu kecil, saya tinggal dekat pantai.
examples.english: When I was little, I lived near the beach.

gap.why: A time in the past takes waktu, and waktu kecil is the set way to say as a child.

examples.indonesian: Waktu saya di Bali, cuacanya panas sekali.
examples.english: When I was in Bali, the weather was really hot.

gap.after: saya di Bali, cuacanya panas sekali.
gap.why: The trip has already happened, so waktu; kalau would make it if or whenever I'm in Bali.

examples.indonesian: Saya kenal suami saya waktu kuliah.
examples.english: I met my husband when I was at university.

gap.why: waktu kuliah: at the time I was at university. When it's the same person, no subject is needed after waktu.

examples.indonesian: Waktu kami sampai, filmnya sudah mulai.
examples.english: When we got there, the film had already started.

gap.note: Ketika means the same. It's more common in writing and when telling a story.
gap.why: Arriving was a one-off moment in the past: waktu.
